title: Application for Building Permit
description: Requirements and steps for securing a building permit from the Office of the Building Official (OBO) of Dipolog City, filed together with the locational clearance and fire safety evaluation clearance.
schedule: Monday to Friday, except holidays. Exact office hours are not stated in the Citizen's Charter, so call ahead.

items: Five (5) copies of the properly filled-out and notarized Unified Application Form for Building Permit, Locational Clearance and Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (Office of the Building Official)

Five (5) sets of design plans and other documents prepared, signed and sealed by duly licensed professionals (architectural, structural, plumbing/sanitary, electrical, mechanical). The Charter specifies A3 size for buildings up to three storeys or up to 1,200 sq m floor area, and A1 for larger buildings
Five (5) copies of the Bill of Materials, signed and sealed by a Civil Engineer, notarized
Five (5) copies of the Standard Specifications, signed and sealed by a Civil Engineer
Structural design and analysis, signed and sealed by a Civil/Structural Engineer
Soil load/boring test for buildings three (3) storeys and higher
Certified true copy of the OCT/TCT on file with the Registry of Deeds
Updated Tax Declaration
Current Real Property Tax receipt
Tax Clearance issued by the City Treasurer
Sketch plan of the lot, signed and sealed by a Geodetic Engineer

If the applicant is not the owner: notarized Deed of Absolute Sale/Contract of Lease; notarized certification from the land owner of no objection to the construction; Extrajudicial Partition with approved subdivision plan; or Declaration of Heirship with waiver of rights
Natural Water Passageway Clearance (City Planning and Development Office)
DPWH road right-of-way / water rights clearance, if along highways or waterways
DOLE Occupational Safety and Health Standards (OSHS) clearance, for structures worth more than ₱200,000
As the need arises: CAAP height clearance (if within a 2-kilometer radius of the runway), ECC, NTC clearance, DOH clearance, NGCP clearance (if under a main transmission line)
Barangay Locational Clearance (plans and designs signed by the Barangay Chairman)

requirements.groupName: Additional Requirements for Locational Clearance (where applicable)
items: Certificate of Height Clearance from the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines
Clearance from the property manager/administrator or homeowners association, if in an existing subdivision or condominium
Permit from the National Water Resources Board, if the project has groundwater extraction
Drainage Impact Statement, for major developments
Socio-Economic Impact Statement, if the project has large employment
Initial Environmental Examination (IEE) certified by the DENR, for industrial facilities
Water Management Plan, for heavy water-using facilities
Historic Site/Facility Development Statement, for historic sites or facilities
Traffic Impact Statement, for potential traffic-generating developments
Notarized Certificate of No Objection from affected neighbors, if the project has a firewall/abutment on any side
Line and Grade Clearance from the City Engineer's Office, if affected by road widening and construction
Waterways Clearance from the City Planning and Development Office, if within the Flood Overlay Zone
Soil test, if within the Liquefaction Overlay Zone

procedures.clientAction: Submit the notarized Unified Application Form and all documentary requirements.
procedures.providerAction: Check plans and documents against the checklist. If complete, assign a reference number and issue a claim stub; if incomplete, return them for compliance.

Record the plans and documents and forward them to the Field Inspectors; evaluators validate ancillary permits and assess electrical and mechanical fees; prepare the Order of Payment (or a Discrepancy Form if issues are found, in which case go back to step 1) and notify the applicant.
procedures.duration: Within 1 day from receipt, plus about 35 minutes
procedures.fee: Based on the Schedule of Fees under the National Building Code

procedures.clientAction: Receive the Order of Payment and all supporting documents.
Pay the fees and charges, then submit all documents with the official receipts to the OBO.
procedures.providerAction: Evaluate and check completeness, then the City Building Official reviews and approves the application; encode and log the approved permit and notify the applicant.
Release the approved building permit and all pertinent documents.

contact.location: Office of the Building Official, Ground Floor, Dipolog City Hall

notes: Total processing time per the Charter: 1 day, 2 hours and 5 minutes.
Only complete and compliant applications are accepted. Fasten all forms, plans and reports in a long folder (5 sets) and include the checklist.
Keep your claim stub: the office follows a "No claim stub, no release" policy.
A 100% surcharge is imposed on anyone who builds, repairs, installs, alters or changes the use or occupancy of a building without a permit (Sec. 25.2, Rule III, National Building Code / PD 1096).

reference.title: City of Dipolog Citizen's Charter 2022 (1st Edition)

title: Certificate of Occupancy
description: Get the Certificate of Occupancy from the Office of the Building Official (OBO), certifying that a completed building complies with safety and sanitary requirements before it is used.
schedule: Monday to Friday, except holidays. Exact office hours are not stated in the Citizen's Charter, so call ahead.

items: Four (4) copies of the properly filled-out Unified Application Form for Certificate of Occupancy and Fire Safety Inspection Certificate

Four (4) copies of the notarized Certificate of Completion (Annex H form), signed by the owner/applicant and signed and sealed by the licensed Architect or Civil Engineer in charge of construction (and by the contractor, if the work was contracted), with one set of the issued Building Permit plans and a copy of the Construction Logbook
Photocopies of the issued Building Permit (the Charter lists "Five (4) sets")
Four (4) sets of photocopies of the owner's copy of the issued Fire Safety Inspection Certificate
Four (4) sets of compliant as-built plans reflecting all corrections made on the issued Building Permit plans, signed and sealed by the owner and all professionals involved
Clear 3R photographs of the completed structure showing the front, sides and rear (4 sets)
Yellow Card issued by the electrical service provider

procedures.clientAction: Submit the accomplished Unified Application Form and all required documents; receive a claim stub and leave a contact number.
procedures.providerAction: Receive and check completeness (incomplete documents are returned), assign a reference number, log it and issue a claim stub.

Encode the application and route it for validation of line and grade, and evaluation of architectural, structural, plumbing, electrical and mechanical plans; the Environment Sanitation Division (City Health Office) evaluates sanitary requirements.
procedures.personInCharge: Encoder / Validators / Environment Sanitation Division – CHO

procedures.clientAction: Retrieve the plans and documents and submit them to the other offices.
procedures.providerAction: City Assessor inspects and issues the ARP and Tax Declaration; City Treasurer computes taxes due and collects; City Planning and Development Office validates land use and approves the zoning certification; Building Official inspects for compliance with the Fire Code and National Building Code; Bureau of Fire Protection collects fire fees and issues the fire safety certificate.
procedures.personInCharge: City Assessor / City Treasurer / CPDO / Building Official / BFP
procedures.fee: City taxes: per the Revenue Code of 1997, as amended. Fire fees: per the Fire Code of the Philippines

procedures.clientAction: Wait for site inspection and assessment.
procedures.providerAction: Conduct site inspection within a day from receipt; if compliant, assess fees and prepare and approve the Order of Payment, then notify the applicant.
procedures.personInCharge: Field Inspectors / OBO Assessor / City Building Official
procedures.fee: Based on the Schedule of Fees under the National Building Code

procedures.clientAction: Retrieve the documents and Order of Payment, pay the fees, and submit the documents with the official receipts to the OBO.
procedures.providerAction: Update records, review the documents, and have the permit signed by the Building Official; notify the applicant.
procedures.personInCharge: Frontline Officer / OBO Assessor / Building Official

procedures.clientAction: Receive the approved Occupancy Permit and supporting documents.
procedures.providerAction: Sort and release the documents and furnish copies to other offices.

contact.location: Office of the Building Official, Ground Floor, Dipolog City Hall

notes: Total processing time per the Charter: 1 day, 2 hours and 58 minutes.

reference.title: City of Dipolog Citizen's Charter 2022 (1st Edition)
